measurement: PYTHONPATH=infra/kiwi python3 -m traceability validate — specs + links only, no stand, no network, no test run (scripts/check-traceability-ratchet.py recomputes both numbers from the same package that renders the matrix)

floors.label: claimed (scenario, target) cells with no automation
floors.note: Dropped 40 -> 38 on ref-night-work-02: TASK-CHECK-01 spec corrected from targets: [desktop] to targets: [android] (Maestro flow). The desktop cell is no longer claimed, so it is neither a hole nor a not-claimed cell.

floors.label: declared scenarios with a claimed target and no automation on any target
floors.note: Dropped 17 -> 15 on ref-night-work-02: TASK-CHECK-01 now has a Maestro carrier on android, so it is no longer dark. 16 dark scenarios remain, all sync or auth scenarios with no carriers committed.

floors.label: claimed cells whose spec declares the tier unable to reach them
floors.note: These are counted in `holes` as well, so reclassifying an ordinary hole as unreachable does not move the total — which is the point, and also the hole this floor closes. Without it, marking every unsupplied claim `unreachable` would make the queue look un-actionable while the number stayed at 32, and the cheap move is always the one that leaves the metric alone. The two metrics together mean a reclassification has to be paid for in one bucket or the other. The 6 are the three sync scenarios that are *defined* by a second device (SYNC-INCOMING-01, SYNC-OFFLINE-01, SYNC-PROFILES-01) on both tiers; the rest of the sync area is one-device and stays probe-able. Raised 6 -> 9 on 2026-10-07 by three cells: CAL-SYNC-RECUR-01 on both tiers (needs a second Google account) and CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01 on android only (reaching the 'permission denied' branch requires granting and then revoking READ_CALENDAR through a system dialog, which is an emulator capability rather than a UI assertion; desktop reaches the branch by construction and IS claimed).

known_gaps: The calendar-sync panel carried ZERO test tags until 2026-10-07, which is the concrete form this gap takes: not a missing test but a missing ADDRESS. No automation could have reached any of its user-visible behaviour regardless of how the ViewModel was tested, so '23 unit-test classes' and '0 carriers' were both true and not in tension. Tags were added alongside TestTags.CalendarSync; and SettingsSwitchRow's testTag parameter — which defaulted to TestTags.Settings.DARK_THEME_SWITCH — is now required, because 15 of its 16 call sites were silently inheriting the dark-theme tag, which makes onNodeWithTag throw on multiple matches.

16 android cells are holes and stay holes on a host with no device: the tier is unverifiable here, and that is more than half the matrix. docs/testing/android-tier-runbook.md is the work order. Because every android hole is 1-for-1, no desktop work can move the total by more than 1; the android tier is where the count is.

The android column of the result matrix is not filled by CI, deliberately. `:androidApp:connectedDebugAndroidTest` ran in no CI job until android-device-tests.yml added it on 2026-10-07 (nightly, tags, manual, and the `run-device-tests` PR label) — but that job produces instrumentation reports, not Maestro scenario results, so it does not move this column. `traceability results --maestro` would need a `scenario:` tag on every flow that claims android — 18 of 19 specs claim it and exactly one flow (TASK-REC-01) carries the tag. CI therefore normalises `--targets desktop` only, so the android cells read as a deliberate `not-run` instead of looking like a measurement that happened to be empty. To close it, tag the flows — the instrumentation job is necessary but not sufficient, which is why the gap stays. See docs/decisions/2026-10-07-the-instrumentation-tier-ran-in-no-ci-job.md.
